question: Namitha gives a 20% discount on all things in her shop and yet makes a profit of 12%. What is the cost price of an item with marked price of ₹280?
solution:
Given:

Profit = 12%

Discount = 20%

Marked Price = ₹280

Formula Used:

MP/CP = (100 + Profit%)/(100 - Discount%)

Calculations:

MP/CP = (100 + Profit%)/(100 - Discount%)

⇒ 280/CP = (100 + 12)/(100 - 20)

⇒ 280/CP = (112)/(80)

⇒ 280/CP = 7/5

⇒ CP = 5/7 × 280

⇒ CP = ₹200

∴ The answer is **₹200**.

Ratio of M.P. to S.P. = 5 : 4 }×₇

Profit % = 12% = 3/25

Ratio of C.P. to S.P. = 25 : 28

So, combined ratio of C.P: S.P : M.P. = 25 : 28 : 35

⇒ 35 units = Rs. 280

⇒ 25 units = (280/35) × 25 = Rs. 200
